heroHeadline: Russia Fires 216 Drones Hours After Ceasefire Ends — Kyiv Hit, 1 Killed; Kremlin Confirms No Plan to End War; Diplomacy at Impasse
heroSubtitle: Russia launched 216 Shahed loitering munitions at Ukraine overnight on May 11–12 — its first major barrage after the 3-day Victory Day ceasefire (May 9–11) expired. Ukraine's air force intercepted 192 of 216 drones, but at least 1 person was killed and 6 injured. In Kyiv, drone debris struck a 16-storey residential building in the Obolon district. Zelensky declared: 'Russia itself chose to end the partial silence.' Ukraine's Foreign Minister Sybiha said Ukraine had proposed extending the ceasefire; Moscow refused and escalated. The Kremlin separately confirmed there are no 'specifics' on ending the war — deflating any hope that the 3-day truce would evolve into sustained diplomacy. The 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange promised as part of the ceasefire remains unexecuted. Russia has now lost an estimated 1,343,160 military personnel since Feb. 24, 2022. Day 1,538 of the full-scale invasion.
